## Comfort with Different Factors by Ethnicity and Country of Residence {#sec-ethnicity-subgroup .appendix}

::: {#suppfig-ethnicity-self-comfort-factor}
```{r}
#| label: suppfig-ethnicity-self-comfort-factor
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

factors_to_show <- c("Race/ethnicity", "Country of origin", "ZIP or Postal Code")

ethnicity_categories <- c(
  "African" = "African \\(",
  "African American" = "African American",
  "Caribbean" = "Caribbean",
  "East Asian" = "East Asian",
  "Hispanic/Latino" = "Hispanic",
  "Indigenous" = "Indigenous",
  "Middle Eastern/\nNorth African" = "Middle Eastern",
  "South Asian" = "(?<!east )South Asian",
  "Southeast Asian" = "Southeast Asian",
  "White" = "White"
)

comfort_df_selfeth <- responses |>
  filter(!is.na(`demo-ethnicity`)) |>
  select(`demo-ethnicity`, all_of(factor_vars)) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(factor_vars), names_to = "factor_var", values_to = "comfort") |>
  mutate(
    factor = factor_labels[match(factor_var, factor_vars)],
    comfort = factor(comfort, levels = comfort_levels)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(comfort), factor %in% factors_to_show) |>
  select(-factor_var)

# Expand: each respondent counted once per ethnicity they selected
comfort_df_selfeth <- comfort_df_selfeth |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(eth_list = list(names(ethnicity_categories)[
    sapply(ethnicity_categories, \(pat) str_detect(`demo-ethnicity`, pat))
  ])) |>
  ungroup() |>
  unnest(eth_list) |>
  rename(SelfEthnicity = eth_list) |>
  select(-`demo-ethnicity`)

comfort_summary_selfeth <- comfort_df_selfeth |>
  count(SelfEthnicity, factor, comfort) |>
  ungroup() |>
  complete(SelfEthnicity, factor, comfort, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  filter(factor %in% factors_to_show) |>
  group_by(SelfEthnicity, factor) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) |>
  ungroup()

# Order by net comfort with race/ethnicity
selfeth_order <- comfort_summary_selfeth |>
  filter(factor == "Race/ethnicity") |>
  mutate(side = case_when(
    comfort %in% c("Somewhat comfortable", "Extremely comfortable") ~ "pos",
    comfort %in% c("Somewhat uncomfortable", "Extremely uncomfortable") ~ "neg",
    TRUE ~ "neutral"
  )) |>
  group_by(SelfEthnicity) |>
  summarise(net = sum(pct[side == "pos"]) - sum(pct[side == "neg"]), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(net)) |>
  pull(SelfEthnicity)

comfort_plot_selfeth <- comfort_summary_selfeth |>
  mutate(SelfEthnicity = factor(SelfEthnicity, levels = selfeth_order)) |>
  group_by(SelfEthnicity, factor) |>
  mutate(
    neutral_pct = pct[comfort == "Neither comfortable nor uncomfortable"],
    xmin = case_when(
      comfort == "Extremely uncomfortable" ~
        -(pct[comfort == "Extremely uncomfortable"] +
          pct[comfort == "Somewhat uncomfortable"] +
          neutral_pct / 2),
      comfort == "Somewhat uncomfortable" ~
        -(pct[comfort == "Somewhat uncomfortable"] + neutral_pct / 2),
      comfort == "Neither comfortable nor uncomfortable" ~ -(neutral_pct / 2),
      comfort == "Somewhat comfortable" ~ neutral_pct / 2,
      comfort == "Extremely comfortable" ~
        neutral_pct / 2 + pct[comfort == "Somewhat comfortable"]
    ),
    xmax = xmin + pct
  ) |>
  ungroup()

net_labels_selfeth <- comfort_plot_selfeth |>
  group_by(SelfEthnicity, factor) |>
  summarise(
    net = sum(pct[comfort %in% c("Somewhat comfortable", "Extremely comfortable")]) -
          sum(pct[comfort %in% c("Somewhat uncomfortable", "Extremely uncomfortable")]),
    x_end = max(xmax),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(comfort_plot_selfeth, aes(y = SelfEthnicity, xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, fill = comfort)) +
  geom_rect(aes(ymin = as.numeric(SelfEthnicity) - 0.35,
                ymax = as.numeric(SelfEthnicity) + 0.35)) +
  geom_text(aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = SelfEthnicity,
                label = ifelse(abs(xmax - xmin) > 8, sprintf("%.1f%%", pct), "")),
            size = 2.5) +
  geom_text(data = net_labels_selfeth,
            aes(x = x_end + 2, y = SelfEthnicity, label = sprintf("%+.1f%%", net)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3, hjust = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Extremely uncomfortable" = "#d73027",
      "Somewhat uncomfortable"  = "#fc8d59",
      "Neither comfortable nor uncomfortable" = "#cccccc",
      "Somewhat comfortable"    = "#91bfdb",
      "Extremely comfortable"   = "#4575b4"
    ),
    name = NULL,
    breaks = comfort_levels
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(abs(x), "%"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(factor, levels = factors_to_show), ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE)) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

Comfort with race/ethnicity, country of origin, and ZIP or postal code as calculator factors, compared across self-reported ethnicity groups (multiple selections allowed). Respondents who selected multiple ethnicities are counted in each group they identified with. Ethnicity groups are ordered from least to most comfortable with race/ethnicity. Bars extend rightward for comfortable responses and leftward for uncomfortable responses, with neutral responses centred at zero. Net comfort is shown to the right of each bar.

```{r}
#| label: suppfig-ethnicity-comfort-factor
#| fig-width: 10

comfort_df_eth <- responses |>
  filter(!is.na(Ethnicity)) |>

  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(factor_vars), names_to = "factor_var", values_to = "comfort") |>

    factor = factor_labels[match(factor_var, factor_vars)],
    comfort = factor(comfort, levels = comfort_levels)
  ) |>

  ungroup()

# Order ethnicity by net comfort with race/ethnicity

  filter(factor == "Race/ethnicity") |>
  mutate(side = case_when(
    comfort %in% c("Somewhat comfortable", "Extremely comfortable") ~ "pos",
    comfort %in% c("Somewhat uncomfortable", "Extremely uncomfortable") ~ "neg",
    TRUE ~ "neutral"
  )) |>
  group_by(Ethnicity) |>
  summarise(net = sum(pct[side == "pos"]) - sum(pct[side == "neg"]), .groups = "drop") |>

comfort_plot_eth <- comfort_summary_eth |>

    neutral_pct = pct[comfort == "Neither comfortable nor uncomfortable"],

      comfort == "Extremely uncomfortable" ~
        -(pct[comfort == "Extremely uncomfortable"] +
          pct[comfort == "Somewhat uncomfortable"] +
          neutral_pct / 2),
      comfort == "Somewhat uncomfortable" ~
        -(pct[comfort == "Somewhat uncomfortable"] + neutral_pct / 2),
      comfort == "Neither comfortable nor uncomfortable" ~ -(neutral_pct / 2),
      comfort == "Somewhat comfortable" ~ neutral_pct / 2,
      comfort == "Extremely comfortable" ~
        neutral_pct / 2 + pct[comfort == "Somewhat comfortable"]
    ),
    xmax = xmin + pct
  ) |>
  ungroup()

net_labels_eth <- comfort_plot_eth |>

  summarise(
    net = sum(pct[comfort %in% c("Somewhat comfortable", "Extremely comfortable")]) -
          sum(pct[comfort %in% c("Somewhat uncomfortable", "Extremely uncomfortable")]),
    x_end = max(xmax),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(comfort_plot_eth, aes(y = Ethnicity, xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, fill = comfort)) +
```

Comfort with race/ethnicity, country of origin, and ZIP or postal code as calculator factors, compared across ethnicity groups (Prolific platform categories). Ethnicity groups are ordered from least to most comfortable with race/ethnicity. Bars extend rightward for comfortable responses and leftward for uncomfortable responses, with neutral responses centred at zero. Net comfort is shown to the right of each bar.
:::

::: {#suppfig-never-use-by-ethnicity}
```{r}
#| label: suppfig-never-use-by-ethnicity
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

make_never_use_diverging <- function(df, group_col) {
  summary_df <- df |>
    count(!!sym(group_col), response = `rep-diao_4`) |>
    ungroup() |>
    complete(!!sym(group_col), response = factor(likert_levels, levels = likert_levels),
             fill = list(n = 0)) |>
    group_by(!!sym(group_col)) |>
    mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) |>
    ungroup()

  # Order by net agreement
  grp_order <- summary_df |>
    mutate(side = case_when(
      response %in% c("Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree") ~ "pos",
      response %in% c("Somewhat disagree", "Strongly disagree") ~ "neg",
      TRUE ~ "neutral"
    )) |>
    group_by(!!sym(group_col)) |>
    summarise(net = sum(pct[side == "pos"]) - sum(pct[side == "neg"]), .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(desc(net)) |>
    pull(!!sym(group_col))

  plot_df <- summary_df |>
    mutate(!!group_col := factor(!!sym(group_col), levels = grp_order),
           response = factor(response, levels = likert_levels)) |>
    group_by(!!sym(group_col)) |>
    mutate(
      neutral_pct = pct[response == "Neither agree nor disagree"],
      xmin = case_when(
        response == "Strongly disagree" ~
          -(pct[response == "Strongly disagree"] +
            pct[response == "Somewhat disagree"] +
            neutral_pct / 2),
        response == "Somewhat disagree" ~
          -(pct[response == "Somewhat disagree"] + neutral_pct / 2),
        response == "Neither agree nor disagree" ~ -(neutral_pct / 2),
        response == "Somewhat agree" ~ neutral_pct / 2,
        response == "Strongly agree" ~
          neutral_pct / 2 + pct[response == "Somewhat agree"]
      ),
      xmax = xmin + pct
    ) |>
    ungroup()

  net_labels <- plot_df |>
    group_by(!!sym(group_col)) |>
    summarise(
      net = sum(pct[response %in% c("Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree")]) -
            sum(pct[response %in% c("Somewhat disagree", "Strongly disagree")]),
      x_end = max(xmax),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  ggplot(plot_df, aes(y = !!sym(group_col), xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, fill = response)) +
    geom_rect(aes(ymin = as.numeric(!!sym(group_col)) - 0.35,
                  ymax = as.numeric(!!sym(group_col)) + 0.35)) +
    geom_text(aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = !!sym(group_col),
                  label = ifelse(abs(xmax - xmin) > 8, sprintf("%.1f%%", pct), "")),
              size = 2.5) +
    geom_text(data = net_labels,
              aes(x = x_end + 2, y = !!sym(group_col), label = sprintf("%+.1f%%", net)),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3, hjust = 0) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "Strongly disagree" = "#d73027",
        "Somewhat disagree" = "#fc8d59",
        "Neither agree nor disagree" = "#fee090",
        "Somewhat agree" = "#91bfdb",
        "Strongly agree" = "#4575b4"
      ),
      name = NULL,
      breaks = likert_levels
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(abs(x), "%"),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}

# --- Panel A: by self-reported ethnicity (multi-select) ---
never_use_selfeth_df <- responses |>
  filter(!is.na(`demo-ethnicity`), !is.na(`rep-diao_4`)) |>
  select(`demo-ethnicity`, `rep-diao_4`) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(eth_list = list(names(ethnicity_categories)[
    sapply(ethnicity_categories, \(pat) str_detect(`demo-ethnicity`, pat))
  ])) |>
  ungroup() |>
  unnest(eth_list) |>
  rename(SelfEthnicity = eth_list) |>
  select(SelfEthnicity, `rep-diao_4`)

p_never_self <- make_never_use_diverging(never_use_selfeth_df, "SelfEthnicity") +
  labs(subtitle = "By self-reported ethnicity (multiple selections allowed)") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE)) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))

# --- Panel B: by Prolific ethnicity ---
never_use_prolific_df <- responses |>
  filter(!is.na(Ethnicity), !is.na(`rep-diao_4`)) |>
  select(Ethnicity, `rep-diao_4`)

p_never_prolific <- make_never_use_diverging(never_use_prolific_df, "Ethnicity") +
  labs(subtitle = "By Prolific ethnicity") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

library(patchwork)
p_never_self / p_never_prolific
```

Agreement with the statement that doctors should never use race or ethnicity in clinical algorithms, by self-reported ethnicity (top, multiple selections allowed) and Prolific platform ethnicity (bottom). Bars extend rightward for agreement and leftward for disagreement, with neutral responses centred at zero. Net agreement is shown to the right of each bar.
:::

```{r}
#| label: suppfig-misclassify-by-ethnicity
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

misclassify_levels <- c("Yes (misclassified)", "Yes (matched)", "Not sure", "No")
misclassify_colors <- c(
  "Yes (misclassified)" = "#d73027",
  "Yes (matched)"       = "#fc8d59",
  "Not sure"            = "#cccccc",
  "No"                  = "#4575b4"
)

recode_misclassify <- function(x) case_when(
  x == "Yes, and it did not match my own choice" ~ "Yes (misclassified)",
  x == "Yes, and it matched my own choice"       ~ "Yes (matched)",
  TRUE ~ x
)

misclassify_selfeth <- responses |>
  filter(!is.na(`rep-misclassify`), !is.na(`demo-ethnicity`)) |>
  select(`demo-ethnicity`, `rep-misclassify`) |>
  rowwise() |>

  ])) |>
  ungroup() |>
  unnest(eth_list) |>
  rename(SelfEthnicity = eth_list)

misclassify_summary_selfeth <- misclassify_selfeth |>
  mutate(response = recode_misclassify(`rep-misclassify`)) |>
  count(SelfEthnicity, response) |>
  complete(SelfEthnicity, response = misclassify_levels, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  group_by(SelfEthnicity) |>
  mutate(
    pct = n / sum(n) * 100,
    response = factor(response, levels = misclassify_levels)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

selfeth_order_misclassify <- misclassify_summary_selfeth |>
  filter(response %in% c("Yes (misclassified)", "Yes (matched)")) |>
  group_by(SelfEthnicity) |>
  summarise(pct_yes = sum(pct), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(pct_yes) |>
  pull(SelfEthnicity)

pct_yes_selfeth <- misclassify_summary_selfeth |>

  summarise(pct_yes = sum(pct), .groups = "drop")

misclassify_plot_selfeth <- misclassify_summary_selfeth |>
  mutate(SelfEthnicity = factor(SelfEthnicity, levels = selfeth_order_misclassify)) |>
  group_by(SelfEthnicity) |>
  arrange(response) |>
  mutate(
    xmax = pmin(cumsum(pct), 100),
    xmin = xmax - pct
  ) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(misclassify_plot_selfeth,
       aes(y = SelfEthnicity, xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, fill = response)) +
  geom_rect(aes(ymin = as.numeric(SelfEthnicity) - 0.35,
                ymax = as.numeric(SelfEthnicity) + 0.35)) +
  geom_text(aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = SelfEthnicity,
                label = ifelse(abs(xmax - xmin) > 8, sprintf("%.0f%%", pct), "")),
            size = 2.5) +
  geom_text(data = pct_yes_selfeth,
            aes(x = 102, y = SelfEthnicity, label = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct_yes)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3, hjust = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = misclassify_colors, name = NULL,
                    breaks = misclassify_levels) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     limits = c(0, 115), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "% to the right of bars = total % Yes") +
  theme_minimal() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE)) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

Proportion of respondents who reported that a doctor, nurse, or clinic staff filled out their race or ethnicity on a form or computer screen without asking them, by self-reported ethnicity (multiple selections allowed). "Yes (matched)" indicates the staff's classification matched the respondent's own choice; "Yes (misclassified)" indicates it did not. Respondents who selected multiple ethnicities are counted in each group they identified with. Groups are ordered from lowest to highest total proportion answering "Yes". The total % Yes is shown to the right of each bar.
:::

Proportion of respondents who reported that a doctor, nurse, or clinic staff filled out their race or ethnicity on a form or computer screen without asking them, by country of residence (countries with at least 20 respondents). ## Comparison with Representative US Surveys {#sec-replication .appendix}

To measure potential bias in our multinational convenience sample, we replicated two questions from representative US surveys. The question "In health and medicine, how much of a problem is bias and unfair treatment based on patients' race or ethnicity?" was adapted from the Pew Research Center, and "In general, do you think you would receive better or worse care from doctors or health care providers who share your racial and ethnic background, or would it not make much difference?" was adapted from the Kaiser Family Foundation (KFF). @suppfig-rep-bias and @suppfig-rep-concordance compare our overall and US-resident survey responses to the representative US samples.

::: {#suppfig-rep-bias}
```{r}
#| label: suppfig-rep-bias
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5

pew_bias <- tibble(
  response = c("Not a problem", "A minor problem", "A major problem"),
  pct = c(28, 35, 35),
  source = "Pew Research Center"
)

our_bias_all <- responses |>
  filter(!is.na(`rep-bias-problem`), `rep-bias-problem` != "Unsure") |>
  count(`rep-bias-problem`) |>
  mutate(
    pct = n / sum(n) * 100,
    response = `rep-bias-problem`,
    source = "Our survey (all)"
  ) |>
  select(response, pct, source)

our_bias_us <- responses |>
  filter(`Country of residence` == "United States",
         !is.na(`rep-bias-problem`), `rep-bias-problem` != "Unsure") |>
  count(`rep-bias-problem`) |>
  mutate(
    pct = n / sum(n) * 100,
    response = `rep-bias-problem`,
    source = "Our survey (US residents)"
  ) |>
  select(response, pct, source)

source_levels <- c("Pew Research Center", "Our survey (all)", "Our survey (US residents)")

bias_comparison <- bind_rows(pew_bias, our_bias_all, our_bias_us) |>
  mutate(
    response = factor(response, levels = c("Not a problem", "A minor problem", "A major problem")),
    source = factor(source, levels = source_levels)
  )

ggplot(bias_comparison, aes(x = response, y = pct, fill = source)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15)), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Pew Research Center" = "#91bfdb", "Our survey (all)" = "#4575b4", "Our survey (US residents)" = "#2a4d6e"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Percentage (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Comparison of responses to "In health and medicine, how much of a problem is bias and unfair treatment based on patients' race or ethnicity?" between our survey (all respondents and US residents only) and a representative US sample from the Pew Research Center. Respondents who answered "Unsure" in our survey were excluded from this comparison as this option was not offered in the Pew survey.
:::

::: {#suppfig-rep-concordance}
```{r}

kff_concord <- tibble(

  source = "Kaiser Family Foundation"
)

recode_concord <- c(

our_concord_us <- responses |>

concord_comparison <- bind_rows(kff_concord, our_concord_all, our_concord_us) |>
```

:::

We also replicated questions from Diao et al., who surveyed a representative US sample on comfort with the use of demographic factors in a cancer risk calculator and attitudes toward the use of race in clinical care. @suppfig-rep-diao-comfort compares comfort with overlapping factors (age, sex, race, and ZIP/postal code), @suppfig-rep-diao-agreement compares agreement with four statements about using race in clinical care.

::: {#suppfig-rep-diao-comfort}
```{r}
#| label: suppfig-rep-diao-comfort
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

# Diao et al. data from figure-2a (collapsed 3-level)
diao_comfort <- tibble(
  factor = rep(c("Age", "Sex/Biological sex", "Race/ethnicity", "ZIP/Postal Code"), each = 3),
  level = rep(c("Extremely or Somewhat\nUncomfortable", "Neither", "Extremely or Somewhat\nComfortable"), 4),
  pct = c(6.5, 13.7, 79.8,   6.8, 14.5, 78.8,   8.8, 16.5, 74.6,   22.3, 23.4, 54.3),
  source = "Diao et al."
)

comparable_factors <- c("fd-factors_1" = "Age",
                        "fd-factors_2" = "Sex/Biological sex",
                        "fd-factors_3" = "Race/ethnicity",
                        "fd-factors_4" = "ZIP/Postal Code")

collapse_comfort <- function(x) {
  case_when(
    x %in% c("Extremely uncomfortable", "Somewhat uncomfortable") ~ "Extremely or Somewhat\nUncomfortable",
    x == "Neither comfortable nor uncomfortable" ~ "Neither",
    x %in% c("Somewhat comfortable", "Extremely comfortable") ~ "Extremely or Somewhat\nComfortable"
  )
}

calc_comfort_pcts <- function(df, src_label) {
  df |>
    select(all_of(names(comparable_factors))) |>
    setNames(comparable_factors) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "factor", values_to = "comfort") |>
    filter(!is.na(comfort)) |>
    mutate(level = collapse_comfort(comfort)) |>
    count(factor, level) |>
    group_by(factor) |>
    mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(source = src_label) |>
    select(factor, level, pct, source)
}

our_comfort_all <- calc_comfort_pcts(responses, "Our survey (all)")
our_comfort_us <- calc_comfort_pcts(
  responses |> filter(`Country of residence` == "United States"),
  "Our survey (US residents)"
)

collapsed_levels <- c("Extremely or Somewhat\nUncomfortable", "Neither", "Extremely or Somewhat\nComfortable")
source_levels <- c("Diao et al.", "Our survey (all)", "Our survey (US residents)")
factor_order <- c("Age", "Sex/Biological sex", "Race/ethnicity", "ZIP/Postal Code")

comfort_comparison <- bind_rows(diao_comfort, our_comfort_all, our_comfort_us) |>
  mutate(
    level = factor(level, levels = collapsed_levels),
    source = factor(source, levels = source_levels),
    factor = factor(factor, levels = factor_order)
  )

# Build diverging positions: uncomfortable left, neither centred, comfortable right
comfort_plot <- comfort_comparison |>
  group_by(factor, source) |>
  mutate(
    neutral_pct = pct[level == "Neither"],
    xmin = case_when(
      level == "Extremely or Somewhat\nUncomfortable" ~ -(pct + neutral_pct / 2),
      level == "Neither" ~ -(neutral_pct / 2),
      level == "Extremely or Somewhat\nComfortable" ~ neutral_pct / 2
    ),
    xmax = xmin + pct
  ) |>
  ungroup()

net_labels <- comfort_plot |>
  group_by(factor, source) |>
  summarise(
    net = pct[level == "Extremely or Somewhat\nComfortable"] - pct[level == "Extremely or Somewhat\nUncomfortable"],
    x_end = max(xmax),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(comfort_plot, aes(y = source, xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, fill = level)) +
  geom_rect(aes(ymin = as.numeric(source) - 0.35,
                ymax = as.numeric(source) + 0.35)) +
  geom_text(aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = source,
                label = ifelse(abs(xmax - xmin) > 5, sprintf("%.1f%%", pct), "")),
            size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = net_labels,
            aes(x = x_end + 2, y = source, label = sprintf("%+.1f%%", net)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.5, hjust = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Extremely or Somewhat\nUncomfortable" = "#d73027", "Neither" = "#cccccc", "Extremely or Somewhat\nComfortable" = "#4575b4"),
    name = NULL,
    breaks = collapsed_levels
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(abs(x), "%"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

Comparison of comfort with the use of demographic factors in a hypothetical risk calculator between our survey (all respondents and US residents only) and a representative US sample from Diao et al. Bars extend rightward for comfortable responses (blue) and leftward for uncomfortable responses (red), with neutral responses (grey) centred at zero. Net comfort is shown to the right of each bar. Responses were collapsed into three categories to match the reporting in Diao et al.
:::

::: {#suppfig-rep-diao-agreement}
```{r}
#| label: suppfig-rep-diao-agreement
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 9

# Diao et al. data from figure-2b (collapsed 3-level)
diao_agree <- tibble(
  statement = rep(c(
    "...as long as my doctor believes\nit is best for my care",
    "...as long as they talk to me\nabout how and why they are using it",
    "...as long as it is recommended\nby practice guidelines",
    "There are no circumstances under\nwhich a doctor should use my race"
  ), each = 3),
  level = rep(c("Strongly or Somewhat\nDisagree", "Neither", "Strongly or Somewhat\nAgree"), 4),
  pct = c(9, 24, 67,   8, 21, 70,   10, 23, 68,   50, 28, 22),
  source = "Diao et al."
)

diao_cols <- c("rep-diao_1", "rep-diao_2", "rep-diao_3", "rep-diao_4")
diao_labels <- c(
  "...as long as my doctor believes\nit is best for my care",
  "...as long as they talk to me\nabout how and why they are using it",
  "...as long as it is recommended\nby practice guidelines",
  "There are no circumstances under\nwhich a doctor should use my race"
)

collapse_agree <- function(x) {
  case_when(
    x %in% c("Strongly disagree", "Somewhat disagree") ~ "Strongly or Somewhat\nDisagree",
    x == "Neither agree nor disagree" ~ "Neither",
    x %in% c("Somewhat agree", "Strongly agree") ~ "Strongly or Somewhat\nAgree"
  )
}

calc_agree_pcts <- function(df, src_label) {
  df |>
    select(all_of(diao_cols)) |>
    setNames(diao_labels) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "statement", values_to = "response") |>
    filter(!is.na(response)) |>
    mutate(level = collapse_agree(response)) |>
    count(statement, level) |>
    group_by(statement) |>
    mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(source = src_label) |>
    select(statement, level, pct, source)
}

our_agree_all <- calc_agree_pcts(responses, "Our survey (all)")
our_agree_us <- calc_agree_pcts(
  responses |> filter(`Country of residence` == "United States"),
  "Our survey (US residents)"
)

collapsed_levels <- c("Strongly or Somewhat\nDisagree", "Neither", "Strongly or Somewhat\nAgree")
source_levels <- c("Diao et al.", "Our survey (all)", "Our survey (US residents)")

agree_comparison <- bind_rows(diao_agree, our_agree_all, our_agree_us) |>
  mutate(
    level = factor(level, levels = collapsed_levels),
    source = factor(source, levels = source_levels),
    statement = factor(statement, levels = diao_labels)
  )

# Build diverging positions: disagree left, neither centred, agree right
agree_plot <- agree_comparison |>
  group_by(statement, source) |>
  mutate(
    neutral_pct = pct[level == "Neither"],
    xmin = case_when(
      level == "Strongly or Somewhat\nDisagree" ~ -(pct + neutral_pct / 2),
      level == "Neither" ~ -(neutral_pct / 2),
      level == "Strongly or Somewhat\nAgree" ~ neutral_pct / 2
    ),
    xmax = xmin + pct
  ) |>
  ungroup()

net_labels <- agree_plot |>
  group_by(statement, source) |>
  summarise(
    net = pct[level == "Strongly or Somewhat\nAgree"] - pct[level == "Strongly or Somewhat\nDisagree"],
    x_end = max(xmax),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(agree_plot, aes(y = source, xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, fill = level)) +
  geom_rect(aes(ymin = as.numeric(source) - 0.35,
                ymax = as.numeric(source) + 0.35)) +
  geom_text(aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = source,
                label = ifelse(abs(xmax - xmin) > 5, sprintf("%.1f%%", pct), "")),
            size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = net_labels,
            aes(x = x_end + 2, y = source, label = sprintf("%+.1f%%", net)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.5, hjust = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Strongly or Somewhat\nDisagree" = "#d73027", "Neither" = "#cccccc", "Strongly or Somewhat\nAgree" = "#4575b4"),
    name = NULL,
    breaks = collapsed_levels
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(abs(x), "%"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))) +
  facet_wrap(~ statement, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

Comparison of agreement with statements about the use of race or ethnicity in clinical care between our survey (all respondents and US residents only) and a representative US sample from Diao et al. The first three statements are prefixed with "I am comfortable with my doctor using my race or ethnicity in clinical care..." Bars extend rightward for agreement (blue) and leftward for disagreement (red), with neutral responses (grey) centred at zero. Net agreement is shown to the right of each bar. Responses were collapsed into three categories to match the reporting in Diao et al.

## Qualitative Codebooks {#sec-codebooks .appendix}

The codebooks below were developed via conventional content analysis of three open-ended survey questions. Two reviewers independently developed and iteratively refined a shared codebook through open coding, then independently applied the codebook to 10% of responses to ensure consistency. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion and consensus, and the remaining responses were coded by one reviewer using the final codebook.

::: {#supptab-codebook-race}
|  |  |  |
|:-----------------:|:----------------------------:|:---------------------:|
| Category | Description | Example(s) |
| Physical traits | Responses referring to physical traits or characteristics, such as skin colour. | *"Colour of your skin"*; *"Race or ethnicity distinguishes people based on complexion. When a person appears darker, they are black"* |
| Ancestry, heritage or lineage | References to ancestry, heritage, or lineage, including where one's ancestors are from. | *"Race or ethnicity refers to ones \[one's\] heritage and bloodline"*; *"To me ethnicity mean\[s\] what region of the world did your ancestors immigrate from"* |
| Cultural or historical background | References to culture, including cultural background or shared culture, as well as historical background or context. | *"A characterization of people based on having a shared culture"*; *"Your history, what makes you who you are"*; *"It means shared history and culture that shape how people are seen"* |
| Biology or genetics | Responses referring to biology, biological characteristics, genes, DNA, or genetic background/characteristics/makeup. | *"Race or ethnicity means my genetic makeup, not where I was born or raised"*; *"Its \[it is\] biological form of identity"* |
| Place of origin | Individual or familial origin or place of origin, including references to the geographical location where one was born and raised. | *"To me its \[it is\] just a way to identify where a person has come from in the world"*; *"Is \[it\] means where your family originated from"* |
| Self-identity | Responses referring to the way an individual identifies themselves. | *"It is what I identify as, and it's who I am as a person"* |
| Community and belonging | Reference to belonging to a community or a group of people. | *"A group someone belongs to"*; *"To belong in a human social group"* |
| Social construct | Referred to race and/or ethnicity as a social construct. | *"Social constructs used to categorize human diversity based on different criteria"* |
| Distinguishes between race and ethnicity | Race and ethnicity were defined and acknowledged as separate concepts. | *"Race means your colour but ethnicity is where you're from"*; *"Race is about physical traits, ethnicity is about cultural identity"* |
| Critique or rejection of race | Responses that explicitly questioned, critiqued, or rejected the concept of race by describing it as meaningless, outdated, or harmful. | *"Race means nothing to me because I don't believe in separate races. There is only one race... Human"*; *"It is an outdated term that continues to be used to group people (often in a discriminatory way)";* |
| Medical relevance | Responses describing race and/or ethnicity with respect to medical or clinical relevance or considerations. | *"My kind of body and maybe some sickness that maybe I have"* |

Codebook for the open-ended question, "In your own words, what does 'race or ethnicity' mean to you? There are no right or wrong answers — we are interested in your personal perspective."
:::

::: {#supptab-codebook-racism}
| Category | Description | Example(s) |
|:-----------------------|:-----------------------|:-----------------------|
| Longer wait time or low priority | References to receiving delayed care, such as having to wait longer or being assigned a lower priority. | *"Put to the back of the line, not treated with urgency"*; *"It's just that they prioritize white people even though we are the first in line"* |
| Differential treatment | Responses referring to being treated or cared for differently, including experiences of poor tone or attitude, poorer quality of care, unfair treatment, racial categorization or profiling based on appearance, and provider knowledge gap that could result in differential access to care. | *"Race plays a big part in how you are treated as a patient here in Canada. There is differential care"*; *"I sometimes felt like quality or more accessible medical assistance were offered to people who had a different race than me"*; *"Took my son to the ER with an allergic reaction that had morphed to a full body rash in hours. We were told by the doctor she was not used to dark skin so couldn't identify what was happening"* |
| Dismissive or neglectful behaviour | Stating that physicians or other providers dismissed, minimized, or did not listen to their concerns, as well as experiencing missed or delayed diagnosis or rushed consultation. | *"I have been to the hospital to have my 3 kids. I have felt 'looked over' and dismissed by the white doctors and had to strongly rebut and stand up for myself. I do feel it had to do with my race"*; *"The doctors (mid-wife) did not take my health concerns seriously and dismissed me"* |
| Physiological assumption or stereotyping | Mentioned experiencing presumptions or stereotypes based on physiological or biological factors such as pain tolerance or different risk for certain diseases. | *"Some doctors think black people are more tolerant to pain"*; *"A doctor remarked the chances of a black person getting prostate cancer was higher compared to that of a white individual"* |
| Social or behavioural assumption or stereotyping | Mentioned experiencing presumptions or stereotypes based on social or behavioural factors such as socioeconomic status, education level, lifestyle, or behaviour. | *"Certain medical staff just think because you aren't caucasian, that you are uneducated when it comes down to medical matters"* |
| Explicit discrimination | Responses mentioning explicit verbal discrimination or racist comments. | *"I was living in a different country and I had to have a surgery and my surgeon kept making racist remarks that made me feel very uncomfortable. Same happened with another doctor who told my son off for speaking with an accent"* |
| Expressed emotional discomfort | Expressed feelings or emotions about their experiences, such as discomfort or having difficulty talking about them. | *"Difficult to talk about these experiences sorry"* |

Codebook for the open-ended question, "Have you ever felt that you were treated unfairly in the healthcare system because of your race or ethnicity?"
:::

::: {#supptab-codebook-reform}
| Category | Description | Example(s) |
|:-----------------------|:-----------------------|:-----------------------|
| Unconditional acceptance | Responses that were positive towards using race and/or ethnicity and did not express any concerns or rejections. | *"It seems fair to consider race"*; *"I think racial classification in medicine has its own specific reasons, given the different living environments of various races, so I am perfectly comfortable with this distinction"* |
| Trust in medical authority | Expressed trust in healthcare providers and researchers to make appropriate decisions about the use of race in clinical decisions, and/or willingness to comply with official recommendations. | *"I trust the doctor's suggestion because they are the experts and know more than I do"*; *"I'm not qualified in the medical field, so I'd prefer to leave it to my doctors. I don't mind, however, of the race, gender or any other trait is used in the statistical analysis; if there are actually some patterns, it's okay to use them for the benefit of the people in my opinion."* |
| Conditional acceptance | Responses that were supportive of using race and/or ethnicity, but conditional to certain considerations (sub-categories below) being met. | *See subcategories below* |
| — *If improves accuracy* | Willing to support the use of race and/or ethnicity if it improves accuracy in diagnosis or other aspects of care provision. | *"Statistically speaking, if there is data that show medical treatment would be better when race is considered, then I am fine considering race as part of the medical diagnosis"* |
| — *Based on specific use case* | Willing to support the use of race and/or ethnicity under certain circumstances or for specific clinical applications. | *"As I am reading, I think it depends on the medical problem and when it can be helpful to reference race in medical questions"* |
| — *Others* | Willing to accept the use of race and/or ethnicity under other considerations than the two mentioned above, such as if it improves fairness, if patients are able to make their own choice, or if patients are given more information at point of care. | *"If the race-specific option is actually better at making predictions, then that is the option I would want. Let the patient make the choice about whether they want to use the inferior or superior prediction calculator, after informing them of the concerns about each method. Make it informed consent. Don't dictate to them or hide from them the options."* |
| Rejection | Responses that rejected using race and/or ethnicity, on the basis of the sub-categories presented below. | *See subcategories below* |
| — *Preference for environmental or social determinants* | Responses referring to having a preference for using environmental or social determinants instead of race and/or ethnicity. | *"Race is a social construct. Any decisions made on race will be unreliable. The factors that mean the most would be environmental, air quality, water quality, education levels, nutritional intake, growth, activities, genetics, government regulations, housing, psychology, etc."* |
| — *Preference for individualized assessments* | Responses referring to having a preference for individualized assessments or approaches instead of race and/or ethnicity. | *"I think each individual should receive fair attention and consideration that isn't focused on things like race, because a person may not fit into the average of their ethnic group"* |
| — *Others* | Rejection of using race and/or ethnicity for other reasons than the two mentioned above, such as preference for using ethnicity over race, preference for using country over race, or general disagreement with the use of race. | *"specifically for blacks. I think ethnicity would be better than race. how does a black caribbean compare to a black american? do the values change? have the studies been done?"* |
| Concerns about using race | Responses that did not reject using race and/or ethnicity, but expressed some concerns with doing so, on the basis of the sub-categories presented below. | *See subcategories below* |
| — *Concerns about overgeneralization* | Expression of concerns about over-generalization or over-simplification of individual differences or other complex factors such as access to care. | *"I am neither for nor against the use of race or ethnicity in deciding factors like these as I understand that people vary genetically. I worry about overgeneralization of races, outliers within races, and effects on mixed race individuals, but I don't think that the use of race or ethnicity is racist in itself. In each of the risk calculations presented, I don't think I have enough information on how a person's race/ethnicity could affect their health, but I always 'follow the science' and am open to having any assumptions challenged"* |
| — *Concerns about bias or discrimination* | Expression of concerns about using race and/or ethnicity potentially leading to bias or discrimination, further disadvantaging certain groups of individuals. | *"Race specific treatment can be very useful because each race has different biological characteristics. The only concern i have is if it might be used for racial discrimination"* |
| — *Others* | Expressed other concerns with using race and/or ethnicity, such as concerns about information misuse or concerns about lack of scientific evidence. | *"I wonder if this is true or it is just a manipulation to gain some info from me"*; *"whether the database of races is large enough?"* |
| Concerns about exclusion | Participants expressing that they did not feel represented in the given race and/or ethnicity categories. | *"I noticed that Mexicans are not included on any of this and are mixed with 'Other' tag"*; *"I am native American and feel that NONE of the categories represents my race"* |
| Concerns about using ZIP code | Expressed concerns or critiqued using ZIP code as a predictor. | *"I didn't get the zip code for demographic instead of race in the previous question"*; *"I find the idea of Zip code to be a useless measure..."* |
| Insufficient information to form an opinion | Responses indicating that they were unable or unwilling to form an opinion about the use of race and/or ethnicity in clinical algorithms due to a lack of information or knowledge. | *"I'd be interested in reading the why behead \[behind\] these decisions when forming my opinion"*; *"Being a south asian, I'm not sure how these race specific calculations will specifically affect me"* |
| Lack of awareness of race in clinical algorithms | Responses sharing that they were previously unaware that race is used in some clinical decision-making tools. | *"No, it was just interesting to participate cause this is the first time i come across information like this"*; *"I didn't know there were equations to determine those types of diseases"* |

## Additional Example Quotes {.appendix}

### Defining Race or Ethnicity {#sec-quote-race .appendix}

The excerpts below are drawn from participant responses to the following open-ended question: "In your own words, what does "race or ethnicity" mean to you? There are no right or wrong answers - we are interested in your personal perspective."

> "For me, race is my physical traits, how do I look. Ethnicity is my heritage, how do I feel. For example, I am Southeast Asian with light brown skin, black hair, light brown eyes. My mom's ethnicity is Batak Simalungun, while my dad's is Batak Tapanuli. I was raised in Simalungun and spent half of my life here. So, I considered my ethnicity as a Simalungunese, although my surname is from Tapanuli."

> "Ancestors/cultural background - I'm Inuit, and native people in general are excluded too often in medical settings/research/general consideration. Indigenous people are so important to medical research and care, and it's unethical to exclude us. Many institutions can and should do better (including you guys, perhaps, since you did not specifically include us); we should not be lumped into a general 'other' group, and as the original peoples of North America, it's wrong on so many levels for research, etc to not consider our medical backgrounds and needs. I think it's very important to consider Black, Asian, etc health systems, family history, etc as well, but please stop excluding the natives!"

> "Race or ethnicity means a whole lot to me. It is one of those factors that signal proximity to a person's identity. Race forms a huge part in my identity. For example, i am a black african male before i am anything else, and this is incredibly important to me because it pours out that i have experiences that are reflective to black people rather than any other race."

> "To me, race or ethnicity means clanship and togetherness, a feeling of belonging to people who share the same culture, traditions, and background. It reflects common roots and a shared identity that connects individuals as part of a community."

> "Race is a social construct used to make some feel superior to others. Ethnicity is where you were born or the cultures you grow up with. For example, if black people have a higher incidence of lung or kidney disease it could be because they live in red lined districts, with poor air and water quality regulations. It's not because they're black that their health is bad, it's because health and safety measures and social constructs have placed them in this predicament."

> "In healthcare, race and ethnicity means 'genetic background'."

> "Mostly just skin color and/or an area of origination of a certain people; but even then... they aren't the same. Are North American indigenous the same as Australian aborigines, or even S. American indigenous people? What about Japanese vs Korean vs Chinese vs Vietnamese vs Filipino? They're quite different, but some of these people are mixed blood as well. Tbh, race or ethnicity is just a generalization for an unknown, and just a guess about where someone may originate from."

> "Race or ethnicity feels like family to me, yet also like distant relatives. When I go back to my hometown, I feel no particular connection because everyone is the same race. But when I go to another country and see someone of my own race, I can't tell you how glad I am to see them. That's how race feels to me—like family, yet like distant relatives."

> "As an East Asian, I do really care and concern about my ethnicity and race, and prejudice/discrimination against my race since I move to an European country. Therefore, race or ethnicity is something threaten me and make me worried and scared in daily life. I do have rather negative image for it."

> "It is a huge part of who I am and dare I say one of the most important. I am German and Native American. The very dichotomy of that mixture has caused so much contradiction not only internally but externally as well. I never quite understood it until I got older. I always felt drawn to choose one. Looking too white to be native and looking too native to be white. I never understood why it mattered because I was still me. Eventually, I came to realize the duality of those perspectives would be exactly what made me who I was. I won't shy away from that."

> "To me, ethnicity is more medically concrete than race. Ethnicity is your personal history, race is a construct used to discriminate by distributing power unequally."

### Algorithmic Reform {#sec-quote-reform .appendix}

The excerpts below are drawn from participant responses to "Do you have any additional thoughts or concerns to share?". This question was posed after participants responded to questions about algorithmic reform based on three revised and one unrevised clinical calculators.

> "The biggest concern I have is the exclusion of Africans. To simply group all Africans in ‘African-American’ will cause a lot of misdiagnosis as these people are very diverse and medical diagnosis cannot be grouped. I think being asked for your country and race and ethnicity is the only way to ensure fairness and more accurate diagnosis."

> "I understand why medical experts want to reduce harm and improve accuracy, but I still feel uneasy about using race or ethnicity in medical calculators because these categories can be imprecise and socially defined. I think it’s important to keep re-evaluating these tools and, where possible, move toward using direct biological or social factors rather than race itself."

> "I am aware that some racial groups are really more likely to have certain diseases like Diabetes. Pacific people, Asians and Hispanics have higher diabetic risk. While Whites have higher risk for skin cancer compared to other races. I think race-specific calculations must be applied depending on the disease or medical condition and careful scientific investigation must be done before implementing them."

> "I’m not particularly concerned of the fact that race/ethnicity could be included in the calculator if this inclusion is statistically relevant and improves the care given to the patients, but I would want for them to be tested against possible harmful biases."

> "The calculators should be based on the country and place that you lived in you might be Asian but you never went there you have been always in New York. If by race it’ll be unfair it should be where the person lives and what are the habits of this person."

> "I’m not qualified in the medical field, so I’d prefer to leave it to my doctors. I don’t mind, however, of the race, gender or any other trait is used in the statistical analysis; if there are actually some patterns, it’s okay to use them for the benefit of the people in my opinion."

### Experiencing Racism in the Healthcare System {#sec-quote-racism .appendix}

Survey participants who answered "Yes" to the question "Have you ever felt that you were treated unfairly in the healthcare system because of your race or ethnicity?", were asked the following: "If you feel comfortable sharing, please briefly describe your experience. You may skip this question if you prefer not to answer." The excerpts below are drawn from participant responses to this question.

> "I remember a hospitalization case of my father in well known government hospital. We remain in queue for 5 long hours for some clinical tests but patients outside of our country and doctors relatives from foreign country got all facilities at instance. It really felt helpless because condition of my father was serious and no doctors or nurses were ready to support."

> "I have experienced situations in healthcare where my symptoms were minimized or not fully investigated. In one instance, a doctor assumed my risk for certain conditions was low based on my race and did not initially recommend further testing, even though I continued to have symptoms. This made me feel that decisions were being influenced by stereotypes rather than my individual health concerns."

> "I felt like I was treated unfairly during labour, like I was expected to endure more pain, plus even during the aftercare my pain was ignored."

> "I was in a hospital after a major loss of blood because of a very heavy menstrual cycle. The were having a difficult time finding a vein and had to stick me multiple times. I was very tired and in a lot of pain to then hear a nurse comment about how the man trying to find my vein should not be so gentle because black peoples skin is thicker. The number of times I've heard this is ridiculous."

> "Because of my middle eastern race, they considered higher chance of possibility of some bad characteristics or having some diseases."

> "I went to a clinic for a tooth ache once and it was really clear that they just wanted to pull it. They said would could save it, but it would be really expensive....as if I couldn't afford it."

> "I feel like I have been to clinics where everyone shared the same fair complexion, and blonde hair & they were very rude to me. Made comments about they see weight struggles in Native Americans (I am not overweight, but they mentioned in passing)." 

> "I consider myself Native American, but there is a lot of mixed blood going back a few generations. In my case, how I am perceived is dependent on the individual person doing the perceiving. Sometimes I am seen as White, sometimes Native, and sometimes they just look me up and down and say, in a very queer tone, 'What are you?'"
